subject: Dedicated SLOs: capacity headroom commitments + mitigation path (Infra/SRE/PM)
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 8:12 AM PST
Subject: Dedicated SLOs: capacity headroom commitments + mitigation path (Infra/SRE/PM)

Sean, Lauren —

We need to close the loop on what Infra is committing to (headroom + response time) to make the Dedicated latency SLO targets real, and to ensure the mitigation runbook isn’t “try to add GPUs” without an agreed timeline.

Can we align today on:
1) Dedicated pool headroom per region (baseline, peak/burst assumptions)
2) During constrained supply or regional incidents, what prioritization is acceptable (Dedicated vs Hosted)
3) What actions SRE can take immediately (routing/overload/fallback) vs what requires Fleet Ops

I’m attaching the current targets working sheet for context. The open row is Dedicated chat/completions p95 and p99 where we’ve had spikes in eu-west.

Attachment: tiered-slo-targets-working-sheet.json (Google Drive export)

- Neha
VP, Infra & Reliability
Redwood Inference


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 8:37 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLOs: capacity headroom commitments + mitigation path (Infra/SRE/PM)

+1. From SRE side the immediate need is a crisp statement we can put into the SLO policy docs + runbooks:

- “Dedicated latency SLO assumes X% headroom per region at steady state”
- “If headroom drops below Y% for >Z minutes, that is an SLO risk and triggers mitigation / incident per error budget policy”

Also: we should be clear about what happens during burst for Dedicated:
- Are we allowed to shed excess Dedicated traffic (429/overload) or must we queue?
- Are cross-region spillovers acceptable for Dedicated customers (and how do we account for it in latency SLI)?

If we can’t guarantee capacity within a region, we should explicitly define the degradation mode (ex: temporary failover to secondary region with increased latency but preserved availability).

Sean
Director, Site Reliability Engineering


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 9:05 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLOs: capacity headroom commitments + mitigation path (Infra/SRE/PM)

Agree we need this nailed down.

From the Dedicated product side, customer expectation is basically:
- Dedicated capacity = predictable latency during normal + forecasted peaks
- Any “we routed you cross-region” scenario is okay only if we communicate it as incident mitigation (and it should be rare)

For SLAs we can’t promise “no overload” if they exceed committed QPS, but we need consistent handling and clear language.

If we’re going to shed, I’d strongly prefer we shed early (429) vs allow timeouts/stream disconnects that look like platform instability.

I can work with Legal on excluding customer-driven overload, but engineering has to be able to detect and classify it correctly.

Lauren
Dir PM, Dedicated


---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 10:14 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLOs: capacity headroom commitments + mitigation path (Infra/SRE/PM)

Here’s a proposed commitment statement (please poke holes):

A) Dedicated regional headroom
- Baseline: maintain 25% compute headroom (measured as schedulable GPU capacity above p95 observed demand over trailing 7 days) in each GA Dedicated region (us-east, us-west, eu-west).
- During peak windows (defined per account forecast + seasonality): maintain 15% headroom.
- N+1: each region must tolerate loss of the largest single host group (rack or k8s node pool unit) without dropping below 10% headroom.

B) Response times / who does what
- SRE can immediately:
  - trigger overload shedding for requests above contracted QPS (returns 429 with “capacity exceeded” reason)
  - adjust routing weights within the same region (sub-pool rebalancing)
  - enable model-variant fallback within the same tier only when explicitly allowed by the customer policy
- Fleet Ops (Infra) within 30–60 mins:
  - expand dedicated pool within region (if warm capacity available)
  - reassign GPUs from Hosted burst buffer to Dedicated (if not in Hosted red budget)
- Infra within 24 hours:
  - add net new capacity (purchase/bring-up) or re-home an account’s reserved slice to a different region (requires PM/CS comms)

C) Prioritization
- When a Dedicated account is within committed QPS and has a contractual SLO/SLA, Dedicated requests are prioritized over Hosted for GPU allocation during shortages.
- If both Hosted and Dedicated are in burn, we prioritize Dedicated first, then Hosted, unless exec override.

This is roughly consistent with the “prioritization notes” doc (attaching).

Attachment: dedicated-vs-hosted-capacity-prioritization-notes.json

Two questions I need answered before we publish:
1) Is 25% baseline headroom achievable in eu-west given current supply? If not, propose a lower number + what target latencies we can still hit.
2) Is “largest host group” the right failure domain for N+1, or should we state it in terms of “node pool AZ” (we can’t over-promise).

- Neha


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLOs: capacity headroom commitments + mitigation path (Infra/SRE/PM)

This is close.

Edits from SRE:
- The headroom measurement should avoid “trailing 7 days” as the only anchor — it can hide step-changes. Suggest: max(p95 demand over trailing 7d, p95 over trailing 6h) or similar.
- For mitigation, I’d like a very explicit stance on “queue vs shed”:
  - For Dedicated over contract: shed early (429) is fine and *should not count* against success-rate SLI if classified correctly.
  - For Dedicated under contract: we should not shed; instead, we should degrade by (1) lowering max_tokens cap per request if customer policy allows, (2) switch to lower-latency quant profile if available, (3) cross-region failover only if in incident mode.

Also: we should document what counts against latency SLO during failover.
- If we do cross-region failover, latency will obviously worsen. We need a decision: either it counts (and we accept burn), or we exclude it as “disaster mitigation” (I’d rather count it to avoid gaming; but call it out in customer comms).

Happy to have Aisha draft the exact text for runbooks and align it to the error budget policy language.

Sean


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 1:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLOs: capacity headroom commitments + mitigation path (Infra/SRE/PM)

On the “counts vs exclude” question: for customer trust, I’d prefer:
- Count cross-region failover against SLO (as Sean said), but we should add language in the SLA mapping that extreme events may trigger regional failover and that we’ll communicate via status page / direct email.

Re: “under contract” degradation levers:
- Lowering max_tokens is OK only if it’s an explicit per-account setting (we can’t silently truncate output in a way that looks like a model bug).
- Switching quant profile/model variant is OK only if it’s the customer’s configured fallback policy.

If we agree on those constraints, I’ll reflect them in the customer-facing comms + SLA mapping draft.

Lauren


---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Feb 7, 2026 at 4:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated SLOs: capacity headroom commitments + mitigation path (Infra/SRE/PM)

Decision + next steps (so we can unblock the doc updates):

1) Headroom commitment
- We’ll publish 25% baseline / 15% peak as the target for GA regions, with the measurement updated per Sean’s suggestion (short + long window).
- For eu-west specifically, I’m not comfortable committing 25% until we verify we can sustain it with current supply. Action: I’ll have Fleet Ops run the last 30d demand vs schedulable capacity analysis by Monday EOD; if we can’t hit it, we’ll either (a) carve a dedicated “burst buffer” inside eu-west or (b) revise eu-west target to 20% with explicit SLO risk thresholds.

2) Degradation policy
- Over contracted QPS: shed early with 429 (classified as “capacity exceeded / customer burst”) — must be tagged so it doesn’t pollute our success-rate SLI.
- Under contract: no shedding by default. Allowed mitigations are (a) intra-region rebalancing, (b) customer-configured fallback/quant profile, (c) incident-mode cross-region failover (counts against SLO).

3) Prioritization
- Dedicated under-contract traffic prioritized over Hosted for GPU allocation during shortage events, unless Hosted is in a severe customer-impacting incident and we have exec override.

Owners
- Sean: have Aisha draft the runbook wording + add the explicit “queue vs shed” section.
- Lauren: ensure SLA mapping doc reflects “over contract shedding” and “failover counts” clearly.
- Neha: validate eu-west headroom feasibility + propose concrete capacity plan.

Let’s sync on Monday after Fleet Ops numbers are in.

Neha
VP, Infra & Reliability
Redwood Inference
